cases.name: dedup-across-runs
cases.proves: one coordinate seen in two different runs collapses to ONE group with run_count 2, while a coordinate seen once stays at run_count 1. The group ordering (run_count DESC) is what puts the recurring one first.

cases.name: occurrences-exceed-run-count
cases.proves: the SAME coordinate twice in ONE review. There is no UNIQUE on (review_id, category, target), run_count counts DISTINCT runs and occurrences do not, so this group carries 3 occurrences behind 2 runs. This is the shape that crashed the endpoint with SQLSTATE 21000.
cases.do_not_tidy: the two rows sharing review 3 / run 3 are the whole case. Giving the second one its own run turns this into a plain dedup case and run_count silently becomes equal to the occurrence count.

cases.name: partial-settle
cases.proves: a coordinate settled in one run and still open in another rolls up to todo on the strength of open_count alone, while each occurrence keeps its own per-run bucket. The done member also carries set_via=issue_close, so the provenance field's omitempty behaviour is exercised in both directions inside one group.

cases.name: rollup-precedence-pairs
cases.proves: every unordered pair of the dismissed > done > filed > todo ladder, one coordinate each. The three pairs WITHOUT a todo member are the only ones that consult the rung ranking at all; the three WITH one prove open_count short-circuits it. The group order here is the open_count tiebreak: all six tie at run_count 2, so the three open ones sort ahead of the three settled ones, each block in first-seen order.
cases.do_not_tidy: the three settled pairs must have NO todo member. Add one and open_count goes above zero, the rollup short-circuits to todo, and the rung ranking those rows exist to test is never consulted. The fixture stays green while pinning nothing.

cases.name: sort-tie-first-seen-order
cases.proves: three groups tie exactly on (run_count 1, open_count 1) and must come out in first-seen order; one group outranks them on run_count and one loses to them on open_count. Dropping the open_count half of the comparator moves epsilon ahead of delta.

cases.name: bucket-filter-all
cases.proves: one row set read at three different ?bucket= values. The filter matches the GROUP ROLLUP, not a member, and the three expected group counts (5, 2, 1) are what make it non-vacuous: a filter that returned everything would satisfy only the first of the three.

cases.name: bucket-filter-todo
cases.proves: one row set read at three different ?bucket= values. The filter matches the GROUP ROLLUP, not a member, and the three expected group counts (5, 2, 1) are what make it non-vacuous: a filter that returned everything would satisfy only the first of the three.

cases.name: bucket-filter-dismissed
cases.proves: one row set read at three different ?bucket= values. The filter matches the GROUP ROLLUP, not a member, and the three expected group counts (5, 2, 1) are what make it non-vacuous: a filter that returned everything would satisfy only the first of the three.

cases.name: preview-ascii-cut
cases.proves: the preview is cut at 280 runes with an ellipsis appended, and it is drawn from the group's OWN FIRST row, which here is row index 1 rather than the first row of the case, and whose text differs from the group's second row. A preview taken from the wrong row is visibly the wrong string, not merely the wrong length. Rune 280 is a 'Z' so the trim cannot touch it.

rows.rationale_md: a later and much shorter rationale for the same coordinate

cases.name: preview-multibyte-cut
cases.proves: a rationale of 300 astral code points is 600 UTF-16 code units, so a code-unit implementation cuts it to 141 runes where a rune implementation yields 281. The odd-offset row puts the code-unit cut MID SURROGATE PAIR, which is the lone-surrogate defect the server's rune count exists to prevent.

cases.name: preview-multibyte-no-cut
cases.proves: 200 astral code points are 400 code units but only 200 runes, so a rune implementation returns the string WHOLE and a code-unit one truncates it. This is the only shape in the fixture that can tell the two apart: past 280 runes both implementations cut, and cut in the same place, so every longer string agrees.
cases.do_not_tidy: these two rows must stay UNDER 280 runes and OVER 280 code units. Shorten them and the case becomes indistinguishable from an ASCII one; lengthen them past 280 runes and both implementations converge and the case pins nothing at all.

cases.name: preview-trim-boundary
cases.proves: rune 280 is a character JS treats as whitespace and Go's TrimRight cutset does not: NBSP, U+FEFF and U+2028 must SURVIVE the trim (281-rune previews), while a plain U+0020 must be trimmed away (a 280-rune preview). The space row is the positive control: without it, a preview implementation that never trimmed at all would satisfy the other three.
cases.do_not_tidy: the space row is not a fourth variation, it is the control. Drop it and 'the trim keeps these three characters' becomes satisfiable by not trimming.

cases.name: sort-stability-13-groups
cases.proves: 13 groups whose run_counts INTERLEAVE 1,2,1,2,... in first-seen order, every group fully settled so open_count cannot break any tie. Go's sort.Slice (pdqsort) insertion-sorts below n=12 and short-circuits on already-ordered input, so an unstable sort is invisible unless all four of these hold at once: at least 13 groups, at least two distinct run_count values, ties within each value, and an input order that is NOT already sorted. Measured: swapping sort.SliceStable for sort.Slice reorders this case, and reorders nothing smaller or tidier.
cases.do_not_tidy: this case is deliberately unrealistic and must stay that way. Reordering these groups into a recency-shaped backlog (all the run_count 2 groups first), or dropping below 13 groups, makes an unstable sort produce byte-identical output and silently deletes the only thing in the repo pinning sort stability. There is deliberately NO mirror-image case for the JS side: Array.prototype.sort has been required to be stable since ES2019, so a JS stability mutation cannot fail and would be decoration.
